task.name: A landed story is written out of its own sprint's record, so its spend is counted in the total while no per-story row explains it
task.story_text:
## Observed

Sprint run `91117cb11b41` was launched over issues 2686 and 2796 and completed.

`forge status` renders both stories as landed, each with its own spend and duration:

```
SPRINT issues-2686,2796  ·  completed  ·  86m  ·  $45.58

LANDED (2 of 2)
  ✓ #2796  $16.38  27m  Issue #2796
  ✓ #2686  $29.20  46m  Issue #2686
```

The work for #2686 did land: it is on `release/v0.16` as commit `4fba49a9`, and the issue
closed at `2026-09-02T06:32:37Z`.

The sprint's own audit disagrees about what it ran. In
`.forge/audits/run-91117cb11b41-sprint-audit.yaml`, `total_cost_usd` is `45.579` — the sum
of both figures above, so #2686's spend is inside the sprint total. But the `specs:` list
holds a single entry, `Issue #2796`, with `cost_usd: 16.38`. There is no story record for
#2686. It appears once in the document, under a different key:

```yaml
closed_dependency_slugs:
- slug: issue-2686
  source: remote_closed
specs:
- path: 'Issue #2796'
  outcome: DONE
  cost_usd: 16.38
```

The audit substrate agrees with the audit rather than with status:

```
$ forge audits show --slug issue-2686
[forge] no audit records found for slug 'issue-2686'.
```

`forge audits show --limit 22` lists `issue-2796` at `2026-09-02T06:33` and no row for
`issue-2686` anywhere in the window.

`forge knowledge-report` is byte-identical before and after this sprint — `Records: 1261`,
cohorts `58 with prior summaries, 4 without, 1199 unclassified`, matched bucket `2 with,
2 without` — so the run contributed nothing to the corpus the report samples.

Net effect: `$29.20` of spend and one landed story are counted in a sprint total while
being individually unaccountable. Every read surface downstream of the substrate — spend
per story, knowledge cohorts, RCA, telemetry — is computed over a set of runs that is
missing one the operator was told completed.

## Expected

A story that a sprint executed, spent budget against and landed is recorded as a story of
that sprint, in the sprint's audit and in the audit substrate, and remains so regardless of
what state the issue tracker is in when the audit is written. Whether a story earns an
outcome record is settled by whether the sprint did the work, not by any condition that the
work itself brings about — a story cannot be written out of the record by the very landing
that completed it, and reclassification of a story into a category meaning "not executed
here" is available only for work the sprint genuinely did not perform.

Spend and accountability do not separate. Where a run's cost is admitted into a sprint's
total, that same run carries an individually addressable record; a total is never composed
of amounts that no per-story record explains. Where a record genuinely cannot be produced,
the discrepancy is reported rather than absorbed, so a reader is never shown a complete
result assembled from an incomplete set.

## Diagnosis
Produced by `forge diagnose` (run `5b186854a880`, artifact `.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-2847-5b186854a880.raw.txt`). The run reached a confirmed, source-verified cause but was classified `CAUSE_FOUND_PARTIAL` and recorded nothing on this issue, so it is attached here by hand; the content is the agent's, unedited apart from formatting.

- **Observed symptom:** A story a sprint executed, spent budget on, and landed (#2686) is counted in the
  sprint's total cost but has no per-story record anywhere: it is absent from the sprint
  audit's `specs:` list, from `forge audits show --slug issue-2686` (no records), and
  from `forge audits show --limit 22`. The sprint's own audit disagrees internally —
  `total_cost_usd: 45.579` sums both stories' spend, but `specs:` lists only
  issue-2796's $16.38 — and the story is instead recorded once, under
  `closed_dependency_slugs`, with `source: remote_closed`, as if it were a dependency
  this sprint never touched rather than a story it ran and landed.
- **Evidence:** .forge/audits/run-91117cb11b41-sprint-audit.yaml: `specs:` has a single entry
  (issue-2796, cost_usd 16.38) while `sprint.total_cost_usd` is 45.579 (both stories'
  cost) and `closed_dependency_slugs` lists `{slug: issue-2686, source: remote_closed}`.
  baseline_check.skip_reason is `reexec_continuation`, with skip_evidence "stories this
  sprint had dispatched and not settled when the re-exec fired: issue-2796" — i.e.
  issue-2686 was already settled (done) before the re-exec, and issue-2796 was still in
  flight when the process restarted. `forge audits show --slug issue-2686` returns "no
  audit records found." Traced mechanically: src/theforge/cli/sprint.py:1188 calls
  `build_resolved_sprint(issues=issues, ...)` unconditionally at the top of every
  process invocation of query-mode sprint launch, including a re-exec continuation.
  src/theforge/sprint/query.py:322-329 fetches each issue's current state and, if
  `IssueClosedError` is raised (issue already closed), drops it from `resolved.stories`
  and adds its slug to `closed_dependency_slugs` — with no check for whether *this
  sprint* is the one that closed it. Because issue-2686 landed and its PR queued auto-
  merge before the mid-sprint re-exec (per the skip_evidence line), by the time the re-
  exec'd process re-resolves the sprint from GitHub, issue #2686 is already closed, so
  it is dropped here. Downstream, cli/sprint.py:1266-1289 builds `slugs` and
  `canonical_refs_by_slug` from `resolved.stories` (which no longer contains issue-2686)
  BEFORE the reexec-only reconciliation (`_resolve_prior_outcomes`,
  `_resolve_story_liveness` at lines 1274-1277) ever runs. Since issue-2686 was never in
  `slugs`/`canonical_refs_by_slug`, that reconciliation — built specifically to recover
  completed work across a re-exec boundary — never gets a chance to act on it. The
  sprint-summary builder's per-story loop (src/theforge/sprint/audit.py:1244 onward)
  only ever iterates `canonical_refs`, which is derived from the same
  `resolved.stories`; a canonical_ref that was never in that set cannot reach any of the
  entry-building branches (`results_by_spec`, `current_story_entries_by_ref`,
  `prior_by_ref`) including the #958 carry-forward branch at audit.py:1430, which only
  carries forward refs that are absent from *this resume's build* but were present in a
  *prior resume's* `canonical_refs` — issue-2686 is absent from both because it was
  filtered at resolution time, upstream of everything that tracks story outcomes.
- **Confirmed cause:** On a mid-sprint re-exec, the sprint process re-resolves its full issue list from GitHub
  before any re-exec-aware reconciliation runs. In query mode, build_resolved_sprint
  (src/theforge/sprint/query.py:322-329) treats any issue that is already closed at that
  fetch moment as a pre-existing "closed dependency": it is unconditionally removed from
  resolved.stories and recorded only in closed_dependency_slugs (source: remote_closed),
  with no check for whether this sprint's own earlier (pre-re-exec) generation is the
  one that closed it. src/theforge/cli/sprint.py calls this resolver unconditionally at
  line 1188, and derives `slugs` / `canonical_refs_by_slug` from its output at lines
  1266-1269 — before the re-exec-only recovery machinery (_resolve_prior_outcomes,
  _resolve_story_liveness, lines 1274-1277) runs, and with no path for that machinery to
  reinsert a slug already dropped at resolution time. Because the sprint-summary/audit
  builder's per-story loop (src/theforge/sprint/audit.py, iterating canonical_refs) only
  ever sees refs present in resolved.stories, a story that finished and closed its issue
  moments before a re-exec is permanently excluded from every per-story record
  downstream, even though its already-measured cost is still folded into the sprint
  total by a different aggregation path. This is the same "recorded execution is
  authoritative over triage classification" hazard runner.py's own comments describe and
  cite as already fixed once, for the git-merge-based skip_merged path (#2150, #1108,
  #2189, see runner.py:5705-5728's _skip_merged_outcome) — but that fix was never
  applied to this GitHub-issue-closed resolution path.
- **Affected code path:** src/theforge/sprint/query.py:322-329 (build_resolved_sprint, IssueClosedError handling
  and closed_dependency_slugs) src/theforge/cli/sprint.py:1186-1198 (unconditional
  build_resolved_sprint call) and :1263-1289 (slugs/canonical_refs_by_slug derived from
  resolved.stories ahead of reexec-only recovery) src/theforge/sprint/audit.py (sprint-
  summary per-story loop over canonical_refs, ~line 1244 onward) — downstream victim,
  not itself defective
- **Fix-success criterion:** When a re-exec'd sprint process re-resolves its issue list and finds an issue closed
  that this same sprint's own (pre-re-exec) generation closed by landing it, that story
  still produces a per-story entry in the final sprint audit's specs: list, is queryable
  via `forge audits show --slug <slug>`, and its cost is not the only thing that
  survives the boundary — the story record does too. An issue closed by something
  genuinely external to this sprint (already closed before the sprint's first generation
  ever looked at it, or closed by an unrelated process) continues to be classified via
  closed_dependency_slugs as today.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 proposes using src/theforge/sprint/prior_landing.py:reconcilable_prior_success as proof that the sprint executed the closed issue. That predicate deliberately accepts both DONE and ALREADY_DONE via PRIOR_SUCCEEDED_OUTCOMES. ALREADY_DONE means the sprint did not perform the work—the runner's _recorded_prior_done explicitly rejects it for that reason. Consequently, a genuinely external closed issue with an accumulated ALREADY_DONE entry would be restored as a normal sprint story instead of remaining in closed_dependency_slugs. The plan also limits restoration to successes, leaving other prior records that prove paid execution vulnerable to the same external-dependency reclassification.
  Suggestion: Use or add a provenance predicate that distinguishes actual execution from ALREADY_DONE. At minimum, require prior DONE plus settled landing for the reported landed-success path; more generally, preserve any prior entry that proves this sprint executed the story while using landing state only to determine reconciliation behavior. Add tests for closed plus prior DONE/landed, closed plus prior ALREADY_DONE, and closed plus a prior paid non-success execution.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 1. Step 1 reinserts the closed issue as a normal (TaskStory, GitHubIssueSource, canonical_ref) tuple and then relies on 'the existing re-exec reconciliation path' to keep it from being dispatched — but the two reconciliation entry points are both conditional on transient state, not on the prior record. launch_guard's RECONCILE_PRIOR_DONE drop (launch_guard.py:285-305) only classifies slugs returned by check_active_worktrees, and the runner's skip_merged triage (runner.py:5705-5741) only fires when git still sees the branch merged. A story that landed, had its PR auto-merged and its worktree/branch cleaned before the re-exec satisfies neither, so the restored story stays schedulable and gets dispatched — re-running and re-spending on already-landed work whose issue is closed, and with story_path/story_text unavailable (the fetch raised IssueClosedError, so no body was ever loaded).
  Suggestion: Do not depend on worktree/branch observation to neutralize the restored story. Carry the restore decision forward explicitly: have Step 1 return the restored slugs (e.g. a reconciled_prior_slugs field on ResolvedSprint or a parallel map out of build_resolved_sprint) and, in the runner, add them to pre_satisfied and skip_slugs alongside the reconcile triage results (runner.py:5729-5744) so they are pre-marked complete in the DAG and excluded from every dispatch/spend path, while _recorded_prior_done/_skip_merged_outcome still stamps the DONE row. Step 4 should assert the restored story produces a DONE specs entry with zero new dispatches when no worktree and no merged branch exist.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried-but-mostly-retired risk 2. finding_registry.description: When a story completed before a re-exec no longer appears in the re-exec's issue query, the final sprint audit can still report the full measured total as complete while specs: omits that story.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
